definition.cn: “横扫” 或 “迅速成功”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from military actions, where it referred to capturing a place quickly and forcefully through a sudden attack. In modern usage, "take something by storm" describes someone or something rapidly and completely taking over a field or community with great success and impact.

examples.en: The new singer took the music industry by storm.
examples.cn: 这位新歌手横扫了音乐业。

examples.en: Her latest book has taken the literary world by storm.
examples.cn: 她的新书在文学界引起了轰动。

examples.en: The new tech gadget took the market by storm.
examples.cn: 这款新科技产品迅速占领了市场。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自军事行动，意指通过突然和迅猛的攻击来夺取某地。在现代使用中，“take something by storm” 常用于描述某人或某事迅速而彻底地风靡某个领域或社区。

definition.cn: 泰然处之，从容应对。
definition.en: This phrase originates from horsemanship and running, where it refers to the ability to handle various obstacles smoothly. It illustratively expresses people's calm and composed attitude when facing difficulties or challenges. It means not getting upset or disrupted by problems, but continuing smoothly.

examples.en: She took the bad news in stride and continued to focus on her work.
examples.cn: 她泰然处之地接受了坏消息，继续专注于她的工作。

examples.en: Even when he faced criticism, he took it all in stride.
examples.cn: 即使面对批评，他也泰然处之。

examples.en: They took the unexpected changes in stride and adapted quickly.
examples.cn: 他们从容应对了突如其来的变化，并迅速适应了。

origin.cn: “Take something in stride” 这个短语起源于马术和赛跑中从容应对各种障碍的能力。它用来形象地表达人们面对困难或挑战时保持冷静和镇定的态度。这个短语表示在困难发生时，不因其而感到沮丧或被干扰，依然能够平稳前行。

definition.cn: “出乎意料” 或 “最了不起” 或 “糟糕透顶”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from 19th-century American beauty contests where the winner would receive a cake as a prize. In modern English, "take the cake" is used to denote something outstanding or surprising, sometimes with a sarcastic tone to indicate something is extremely bad.

examples.en: Her performance truly takes the cake; it was amazing!
examples.cn: 她的表演真的太了不起了；简直令人惊叹！

examples.en: Out of all the mistakes, that one really takes the cake.
examples.cn: 在所有的错误中，那一个真是最糟糕的。

examples.en: I’ve heard some excuses before, but this one takes the cake.
examples.cn: 我以前听过一些借口，但这个真是出乎意料。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于19世纪美国的选美比赛，优胜者会获得一个蛋糕作为奖品。在现代英语中，“take the cake” 则被用来表示某事非常出色或令人震惊，有时也带有讽刺意味，用来指某事极其糟糕。

definition.cn: “发言” 或 “开始讲话”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from formal meetings or debates, where a person would stand up and begin speaking or presenting their opinion. "Take the floor" means that the person is allowed or designated as the main speaker, controlling the proceedings of the meeting or discussion. In modern usage, it can be applied to any situation requiring formal speaking.

examples.en: After the chairman's introduction, she was invited to take the floor and present her ideas.
examples.cn: 在主席的介绍之后，她被邀请上台发言并展示她的想法。

examples.en: The CEO will take the floor to address the company's financial performance.
examples.cn: CEO 将会发言，说明公司的财务表现。

examples.en: When he took the floor, everyone listened attentively to his proposal.
examples.cn: 当他发言时，所有人都专心聆听他的提议。

origin.cn: 这个短语最初用于正式会议或辩论中，指一个人从座位上站起来，正式开始发言或发表意见。“Take the floor” 意味着这个人被允许或指定为主要的发言者，控制会议或讨论的进程。在现代用法中，它可以应用于任何需要正式发言的场合。

definition.cn: “冒险一试” 或 “果断行动”。
definition.en: This phrase comes from the action of diving or plunging into water, signifying the decision to jump from a height into the water. By extension, it describes the resolve and bravery needed to dive into new experiences or adventures, especially in situations fraught with uncertainty or challenges. In contemporary usage, it often relates to making significant decisions, such as changing jobs, relocating, or starting a new project.

examples.en: After years of working in a corporate job, she finally decided to take the plunge and start her own business.
examples.cn: 在公司工作多年之后，她终于决定冒险一试，创业开了自己的公司。

examples.en: They had been dating for five years, so they decided it was time to take the plunge and get married.
examples.cn: 他们已经约会五年了，所以决定该是时候勇敢迈出一步结婚了。

examples.en: Moving to a new city alone can be daunting, but sometimes you just have to take the plunge.
examples.cn: 一个人搬到一个新城市可能会让人望而生畏，但有时你就是需要果断行动。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于跳水或者潜水的动作，表示从高处跳入水中的决定。引申意义上，这个表达表述了跳入新体验或冒险的决心和勇气，通常在面对不确定或具有挑战性的情况时使用。现代人也用它来形容做重大决策，比如换工作、搬家或开始新项目。

title: Take the wind out of your sails

definition.cn: “让你泄气” 或 “使你气馁”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from sailing. When one ship blocks the wind of another ship, the latter loses speed and momentum. "Take the wind out of your sails" is used metaphorically to describe situations where someone is discouraged or loses confidence or motivation.

examples.en: Her criticism really took the wind out of my sails.
examples.cn: 她的批评真的让我很泄气。

examples.en: When I found out I didn't get the job, it took the wind out of my sails.
examples.cn: 当我知道自己没得到那份工作时，真的很泄气。

examples.en: The unexpected death of his mentor took the wind out of his sails.
examples.cn: 导师的意外去世让他倍感失落。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自航海术语。当一艘船被其他船只阻挡风力时，它的速度会减慢，失去动力。“Take the wind out of your sails” 被用来比喻一个人被打击，失去了动力或信心。

definition.cn: “被欺骗” 或 “受骗上当”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in American slang from the 1920s, originally referring to criminals taking victims to isolated places. Nowadays, it is widely used to describe situations where someone has been deceived or taken advantage of by another person.

examples.en: He realized he'd been taken for a ride when the car he bought broke down the next day.
examples.cn: 当他买的车第二天就坏了时，他意识到自己被骗了。

examples.en: I can't believe she took us for a ride; the tickets she sold us were fake.
examples.cn: 我真不敢相信她骗了我们，她卖给我们的票是假的。

examples.en: The investors felt they were taken for a ride when the company's CEO vanished with all the funds.
examples.cn: 当那家公司的CEO带着所有资金消失时，投资者们觉得自己被骗了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国 20 世纪 20 年代的俚语，原指犯罪分子把受害者带到偏僻地方。如今它广泛用于描述一个人被某人欺骗或者利用的情形。

definition.cn: “滔滔不绝” 或 “说话特别快”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the United States and first appeared in the 19th century. It compares the speed of talking to lightning because "blue streak" literally means a high-speed blue line, symbolizing great speed. Therefore, "talk a blue streak" means to talk very fast, often with strong passion and excitement.

examples.en: When she gets nervous, she tends to talk a blue streak.
examples.cn: 她一紧张就会滔滔不绝地说话。

examples.en: He can talk a blue streak about his favorite hobby for hours.
examples.cn: 他可以滔滔不绝地谈论他最喜欢的爱好好几个小时。

examples.en: At the meeting, he was so excited that he started to talk a blue streak.
examples.cn: 在会议上，他非常兴奋，开始滔滔不绝地讲话。

origin.cn: 这个成语来源于美国，最早出现在19世纪。它把说话的速度比作闪电的速度，因为 “blue streak” 字面意思为高速的蓝色光线，象征速度极快。因此，“talk a blue streak” 意指以极快的速度说话，通常伴随着很强的激情和兴奋。

definition.cn: “谈论的热点” 或 “城中话题”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from old town settings where news and interesting events would quickly spread and become the subject of everyone's conversations. "Talk of the town" is used to describe something or someone that has attracted a lot of attention and is the current popular topic.

examples.en: The new restaurant in town is the talk of the town.
examples.cn: 城里那家新开的餐馆成了大家谈论的热点。

examples.en: Her amazing performance made her the talk of the town.
examples.cn: 她的精彩表演使她成了城中的话题。

examples.en: The scandal quickly became the talk of the town.
examples.cn: 那个丑闻很快就成了大家议论的话题。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古老的城镇环境，在那里，新闻和有趣的事情会迅速传播并成为人们茶余饭后的谈资。“Talk of the town” 用来形容某事或某人引起了广泛关注和讨论，成为当前的热门话题。

definition.cn: “说得某人耳朵都快掉了” 或 “喋喋不休地说话”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the idea of someone talking excessively and lengthily to the point where the listener feels overwhelmed or exhausted. It vividly illustrates a situation where the speaker continues to talk incessantly, making the listener feel as if their ears might fall off. It's often used humorously or exaggeratedly to describe someone who talks a lot or at length in a particular conversation.

examples.en: He can really talk your ear off about his new hobby.
examples.cn: 他可以滔滔不绝地讲他的新爱好，说得你耳朵都快掉了。

examples.en: I like Sarah, but she will talk your ear off if you ask about her pets.
examples.cn: 我喜欢莎拉，但如果你问起她的宠物，她会一直说个没完，让你耳朵都快掉了。

examples.en: After the meeting, Bob talked my ear off about his weekend plans.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，鲍勃一直在谈论他的周末计划，说得我耳朵都快掉了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于对某人进行过度和冗长的说话，直到对方感到厌烦或疲惫。它形象地描绘了说话者不停地说话，以至于听者感觉自己的耳朵都快掉了。在使用时，通常带有轻微的幽默和夸张意味，适用于描述某人的 Gesprächigkeit 或在特定谈话中的冗长。

definition.cn: “胡说八道” 或 “不懂装懂”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in 19th-century America and initially meant someone was speaking nonsensically or without foundation. It usually has a pejorative connotation, indicating that someone is speaking without knowledge or experience, essentially talking nonsense.

examples.en: He doesn't know anything about cars; he's just talking through his hat.
examples.cn: 他对汽车一无所知，他只是在胡说八道。

examples.en: I wouldn't believe him, I think he's talking through his hat.
examples.cn: 我不会相信他，我认为他在不懂装懂。

examples.en: Stop talking through your hat and do some research before making such claims.
examples.cn: 别再胡说八道了，在做出这样的声明之前先做些研究。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自19世纪美国，最初的意思是指某人空谈或说一些没根据的话。它通常带有贬义，表示某人说话时缺乏知识或经验，完全是在瞎说。

title: Talk to someone like a Dutch uncle

definition.cn: “像荷兰叔叔一样对某人谈话” 或 “严厉地批评或劝导”。
definition.en: This idiom has a somewhat debated origin but is generally believed to come from Dutch culture, where an uncle is often seen as a family member who can provide stern yet fair criticism and guidance. Therefore, when someone "talks to you like a Dutch uncle," it means they are giving you frank, stern advice or criticism, intended for your own good.

examples.en: When I was slacking off, my mentor sat me down and talked to me like a Dutch uncle.
examples.cn: 当我松懈时，我的导师严厉地批评了我，就像荷兰叔叔一样。

examples.en: She talked to him like a Dutch uncle about the importance of being responsible.
examples.cn: 她就责任的重要性严厉地劝导了他，就像荷兰叔叔一样。

examples.en: Sometimes you need someone who will talk to you like a Dutch uncle to keep you on track.
examples.cn: 有时候你需要一个像荷兰叔叔一样的人来让你保持正轨。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源带有一些争议，但普遍认为是源自荷兰文化中的亲属关系中，叔叔通常被认为是家庭中能给予严厉但是公正的批评和劝导的角色。因此，当有人 “像荷兰叔叔一样对你说话” 时，意味着他们正直言不讳、严厉但诚恳地以你的利益为出发点进行劝告或批评。

definition.cn: “别跟我说” 或 “我不想听”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the slang of the 1990s in the United States, typically accompanied by a hand gesture with the palm facing outward, symbolizing a refusal to listen or impatience. Over time, "Talk to the hand" became a verbal expression used to indicate that someone is uninterested and does not want to hear what the other person is saying.

examples.en: When he started arguing, she just said, "Talk to the hand."
examples.cn: 当他开始争论时，她只说了一句，“别跟我说。”

examples.en: If you're going to complain again, just talk to the hand.
examples.cn: 如果你又要抱怨，那就别跟我说。

examples.en: I tried to explain, but he just told me, "Talk to the hand."
examples.cn: 我试图解释，但他只是对我说，“我不想听。”

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于上世纪90年代的美国俚语，通常是作为一种表示不耐烦或不愿意听某人说话的手势动作。在说这句话时，人们会将手掌向外平伸，表示拒绝交流和不满。随着时间的推移，这个短语渐渐成为一种口头表达，用来表示某人对他人的话语不感兴趣且不愿意听。

definition.cn: “直截了当” 或 “开门见山”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the United States and became popular in the early 19th century. Initially, it referred to serious and earnest discussions about trading turkeys between European settlers and Native Americans. It now signifies getting straight to the point in conversations.

examples.en: Let's talk turkey about the deal and see if we can agree.
examples.cn: 让我们开门见山地谈谈这个交易，看能否达成一致。

examples.en: We should talk turkey instead of avoiding the real issues.
examples.cn: 我们应该直截了当地讨论，而不是避开真正的问题。

examples.en: It's time to talk turkey about how to improve our project efficiency.
examples.cn: 是时候开门见山地讨论如何提高我们的项目效率了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国，在19世纪初非常流行。当时，欧洲定居者和印第安人之间经常进行火鸡贸易。最初，它意味着严肃而认真地讨论交易，因此带有直接和诚实的对话的意味。如今，“talk turkey” 用于表示在谈话中直奔主题、直接了当。

definition.cn: “谈论工作” 或 “谈论行业内的事情”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from shopkeepers and artisans gathering after shop hours to discuss business and craft matters. Hence, it is used to describe people discussing work or industry-specific topics in a social setting, rather than broader or more recreational discussions.

examples.en: Whenever those two get together, they can't help but start talking shop.
examples.cn: 每次那两个人坐在一起，他们都会忍不住开始谈论工作。

examples.en: I wanted to catch up with old friends, but all they did was talk shop.
examples.cn: 我本想和老朋友叙旧，但他们只是一直在谈论工作。

examples.en: Can we avoid talking shop during dinner? Let's enjoy the meal.
examples.cn: 我们晚餐时能不谈工作吗？让我们享受饭菜吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于商店掌柜和工匠在铺子关门后聚在一起讨论生意和手艺问题。因此，它用来描述人在社交场合下只谈论与工作或行业相关的话题，而不是更广泛的或更休闲的讨论。

definition.cn: “艰难的任务” 或 “难以实现的请求”。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to the late 19th century and was originally a sports term used to describe particularly challenging tasks or demands. Over time, "tall order" has come to be used in general contexts to refer to tasks or requests that are exceptionally difficult.

examples.en: Convincing him to change his mind is a tall order.
examples.cn: 要说服他改变主意是一个艰难的任务。

examples.en: Finishing this project by next week is a tall order.
examples.cn: 要在下周之前完成这个项目是一个难以实现的请求。

examples.en: Getting everyone to agree on the new plan will be a tall order.
examples.cn: 要让所有人都同意这个新计划将会是一个艰难的任务。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到19世纪末。原本是一个体育术语，用来描述那些非常高难度的任务或要求。随着时间的推移，"tall order" 被广泛应用于各种场合，形容那些超过常规难度的任务或请求。

definition.cn: “夸张的故事” 或 “荒诞的故事”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the phrase "tall tale," which describes a highly exaggerated or hard-to-believe story. Such stories are usually fictional, often using exaggerated details to capture the audience's attention. In Western culture, these stories are sometimes used for entertainment, particularly in the tradition of oral storytelling.

examples.en: He told us a tall story about how he once wrestled a bear.
examples.cn: 他给我们讲了一个关于他曾经与熊摔跤的夸张故事。

examples.en: That's just a tall story. I don't believe a word of it.
examples.cn: 那只是一个夸张的故事，我一个字都不相信。

examples.en: Kids love to hear tall stories around the campfire.
examples.cn: 孩子们喜欢在篝火旁听夸张的故事。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于 “tall tale” 这个短语，描述高度夸张或难以置信的故事。这样的故事通常是虚构的，往往通过夸大的细节来吸引听众的注意力。这类故事在西方文化中有时被用于娱乐，特别是在口头讲述传统中。

title: Tar someone with the same brush

definition.cn: “同一枚刷子刷所有人” 或 “一概而论”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from maritime practices where tar was used to coat and protect ships. Over time, it has evolved into a metaphor indicating treating everyone the same way, often negatively, based on the actions or characteristics of a few individuals.

examples.en: Just because he made a mistake doesn't mean you should tar everyone with the same brush.
examples.cn: 仅仅因为他犯了错误，并不意味着你应该一概而论。

examples.en: It's not fair to tar all teenagers with the same brush for the actions of a few.
examples.cn: 因为少数青少年的行为就一概而论所有青少年是不公平的。

examples.en: You can't tar the entire team with the same brush because of one person's failure.
examples.cn: 因为一个人的失败就把整个团队一概而论是不对的。

origin.cn: 这个词组源自古代，早期形容在海运中给船只刷沥青以防腐蚀。然而，逐渐演变为一种隐喻，用来描述将个人特质或行为推广到整个群体或其他个体上，即对某人集团或某类事物持有相同的负面看法，不分具体情况。

definition.cn: “就是啊” 或 “可不是嘛”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to convey complete agreement or empathy with someone else's statement. Though the phrase literally seems to be asking for more information, it actually expresses that the speaker has similar experiences or feelings as the other person.

examples.en: "The traffic this morning was terrible." "Tell me about it."
examples.cn: “今天早上的交通糟透了。”“就是啊。”

examples.en: "I can't believe how expensive groceries are getting." "Tell me about it."
examples.cn: “我真不敢相信食品杂货越来越贵了。”“可不是嘛。”

examples.en: "I've been so busy with work lately." "Tell me about it."
examples.cn: “我最近工作太忙了。”“就是啊。”

origin.cn: 这个短语通常用来表示对他人的陈述完全同意或感同身受。虽然短语字面上看似在要求对方提供更多信息，但实际上它表达的是说话者与对方有相似的经历或感受。

definition.cn: “试探” 或 “摸底”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the act of people testing the water with their foot before fully stepping into it, ensuring it’s safe. In modern life, "test the waters" is used to describe making small attempts or investigations before making a significant decision to determine if it’s viable or suitable.

examples.en: We should test the waters before committing to the new project.
examples.cn: 我们应该在对新项目做出承诺之前试探一下。

examples.en: She decided to test the waters by pitching her idea to a few investors first.
examples.cn: 她决定通过先向几位投资人提出她的想法来试探一下。

examples.en: Before launching the product nationwide, the company plans to test the waters in a few select markets.
examples.cn: 在全国范围内推出产品之前，公司计划在几个选择的市场中试探一下。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于人们在进入未知的水域时，通常会先用脚去试探水温和深浅，确保安全后才会进入水中。在现代生活中，“test the waters” 用来描述在做重要决定之前先进行少量的尝试或调查，以判断是否可行或合适。

definition.cn: “正合我意” 或 “正是我想要的”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the feeling when something you eat or drink particularly satisfies your needs or cravings. Modernly, this idiom is commonly used to describe something (especially food or drink) that exactly meets someone's expectations and needs, providing a sense of satisfaction.

examples.en: That pizza really hit the spot.
examples.cn: 那块披萨真正合我意。

examples.en: After a long hike, a cold lemonade hit the spot.
examples.cn: 在长距离徒步后，一杯冰柠檬水正是我需要的。

examples.en: The spicy noodles hit the spot on a cold day.
examples.cn: 在寒冷的日子里，辣面条真是正合我意。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于人们吃东西或喝饮料时，如果某种味道或感觉特别满足他们的需求或想法，会用 “hit the spot” 来描述那种刚好合适的开心和满足感。在现代社会，这个短语通常用来形容某个东西（尤其是食物和饮料）正好满足了某人的期待和需求。

definition.cn: “也就是说”。
definition.en: The phrase is used to further explain or restate what has been said, ensuring clarity and understanding. For example, after providing a complex idea, you might use "That is to say" to rephrase it in a simpler or more straightforward way. It is common in both spoken and written language.

examples.en: He is a polyglot, that is to say, he speaks many languages.
examples.cn: 他是个多语言者，也就是说，他会说很多种语言。

examples.en: The project failed, that is to say, it didn't meet our expectations.
examples.cn: 项目失败了，也就是说，它没有达到我们的期望。

examples.en: We need more time, that is to say, we won't finish by the deadline.
examples.cn: 我们需要更多时间，也就是说，我们无法在截止日期前完成。

origin.cn: 该短语用来进一步解释或重述之前的话，以确保信息清楚明确。例如，当你给出一个复杂的观点后，可以使用 “That is to say” 来重新解释，以更简单或直白的方式说出来。在口语和书面语中都很常见。

definition.cn: “船已经开了” 或 “机不可失时不再来”。
definition.en: This idiom comes from the age of sailing, where once a ship left the port, those who missed it had to wait for the next one. In modern usage, it describes a situation where an opportunity has been missed and is no longer possible.

examples.en: He wanted to ask her out, but now she’s dating someone else. That ship has sailed.
examples.cn: 他曾想约她出去，但她现在已经在和别人约会了。机不可失时不再来。

examples.en: We were considering buying that house last month, but now that ship has sailed.
examples.cn: 我们上个月考虑买那栋房子，但现在机会已经没了。

examples.en: Could we reschedule the meeting? Sorry, that ship has sailed.
examples.cn: 我们能重新安排会议吗？抱歉，已经来不及了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于航海的时代，当一艘船离港后，错过这艘船的人只能等待下一艘。现代社会中，这个表达被用来形容一个机会已经错过，不再可能实现。

definition.cn: “事情就到这里”，或 “事情结束了”。用来表达某件事情已经完全结束或达到了最终结果，没有更多的内容可供补充。
definition.en: This phrase has various speculated origins, but a common explanation dates back to World War II. Soldiers would receive short letters from home, and they would say "That's all she wrote," indicating that there was no more information in the letter. Over time, this phrase became a fixed expression used to signify that something is completely finished or there is nothing more to discuss.

examples.en: After the team lost the final game, that's all she wrote.
examples.cn: 在队伍输掉最后一场比赛后，事情就到此为止了。

examples.en: When he walked out of the room, that's all she wrote.
examples.cn: 当他走出房间时，事情就算结束了。

examples.en: She handed in her resignation letter and that's all she wrote.
examples.cn: 她提交了辞职信，事情就结束了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源有多种说法，一种较为普遍的说法是，来源于第二次世界大战期间士兵们从家收到的简单信件，信中只有一句 “That's all she wrote”（她就写了这些），表示已经没有更多的信息传递给收信人。这句话后来被提炼为一个固定表达，用以形容事情已尘埃落定或没有更多可以谈论的事情。

definition.cn: “这是最后一根稻草” 或 “压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a fable about a camel being loaded with increasing amounts of burden until a small straw finally breaks its back. This expression is often used to describe a situation where a person is dealing with continuous pressure or problems, and finally, one small issue or event causes them to no longer bear, endure, or compromise.

examples.en: When he arrived late again, it was the last straw for his boss.
examples.cn: 当他再次迟到时，这对他的老板来说是最后一根稻草。

examples.en: Her constant complaints were the last straw in their relationship.
examples.cn: 她不断的抱怨是他们关系中的最后一根稻草。

examples.en: Finding out about his lie was the last straw for her.
examples.cn: 发现他的谎言对她来说就是压垮她的最后一根稻草。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于一句寓言，讲的是一个骆驼被逐渐增加的负担压垮，直到最后一小撮稻草终于使它不堪重负。这个表达常用于形容人在面对持续的压力或问题时，最终一个小问题或事件使人再也无法忍受、承受或妥协。

definition.cn: “这真是太棒了” 或 “太厉害了”。
definition.en: This slang phrase originated in the UK and later became widely used in the US, especially in the Boston area. Although "wicked" originally means "evil," in this context it means extremely good or impressive. This usage perhaps evolved through youth subculture language practices, where antonyms were used to create new expressions.

examples.en: That concert was wicked!
examples.cn: 那场演唱会真是太棒了！

examples.en: Wow, your skateboard tricks are wicked!
examples.cn: 哇，你的滑板技巧真是太厉害了！

examples.en: The special effects in that movie were wicked!
examples.cn: 那部电影的特效真是太酷了！

origin.cn: "That's wicked" 是一种俚语，最早起源于英国，后在美国特别是波士顿地区广泛使用。虽然 "wicked" 本意是 “邪恶的”，但在这种用法中却表示极好或令人印象深刻，这种用法可能源自青少年亚文化的语言现象，利用反义词创造新的表达方式。

definition.cn: “掌上明珠” 或 “珍爱之人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Old English. At that time, the word "apple" referred to the pupil of the eye, which was considered the most important part of the eye. Therefore, describing someone as "the apple of my eye" means that the person is very important and precious to you, cherished like the pupil of your eye.

examples.en: My daughter is the apple of my eye.
examples.cn: 我的女儿是我的掌上明珠。

examples.en: He always talks about his son as if he is the apple of his eye.
examples.cn: 他总是谈论他的儿子，好像他是他的掌上明珠。

examples.en: Her little dog is the apple of her eye.
examples.cn: 她的小狗是她的掌中宝。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古英语时期。当时，“apple” 这个词用来指瞳孔，因为瞳孔被认为是眼睛中最重要的部分。因此，形容一个人为 “the apple of my eye” 意味着这个人对你来说非常重要和珍贵，像是你眼中的瞳孔一样珍视。

title: The ball is in your court

definition.cn: “轮到你做决定” 或 “现在由你负责”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from sports like tennis, where when the ball is in a player's court, it's their responsibility to hit it back and make the next move. In daily life, it is used metaphorically to indicate that the responsibility or decision-making power now lies with a specific person.

examples.en: I've given you all the information. Now the ball is in your court.
examples.cn: 我已经给了你所有信息，现在轮到你决定了。

examples.en: We made our offer, so the ball is in their court now.
examples.cn: 我们已经提出了条件，现在轮到他们决定了。

examples.en: After the meeting, the ball is in his court to finalize the deal.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，最终敲定交易的任务就交到了他手上。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于网球等球类运动中，当球在某一方球场时，表示该方需要接球并决定下一步的动作。引申到日常生活中，这句话被用来比喻在某个决策或行动过程中，当前的责任或选择权归某人所有。

definition.cn: “最顶尖的” 或 “最好的”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in American slang in the 1920s and was used to describe anything exceptionally good or of high quality. Its exact origins are unclear, but some researchers suggest that it might just be a nonsense phrase that caught on as a way to humorously describe something outstanding.

examples.en: That new bakery down the street is the bee's knees.
examples.cn: 街道那头新开的面包店简直是最棒的。

examples.en: Her homemade apple pie is the bee's knees.
examples.cn: 她自制的苹果派堪称一绝。

examples.en: I think this new movie is the bee's knees.
examples.cn: 我觉得这部新电影非常棒。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于1920年代的美国俚语，最初用来形容任何特别优秀的事物或人。它的确切起源并不十分明确，但一些研究人员认为这只是一个无意义的短语，它是用来说笑和形容好东西的。

definition.cn: “两全其美”。
definition.en: This phrase means to get the greatest benefits from two different situations or choices without any negative consequences. It can be traced back to the 19th century and emphasizes an ideal, perfect state in which two contrasting things coexist harmoniously.

examples.en: Working from home gives me the best of both worlds; I can be productive and spend more time with my family.
examples.cn: 在家工作让我两全其美；我既能高效工作，又能花更多时间陪伴家人。

examples.en: This hybrid car offers the best of both worlds by being both eco-friendly and cost-effective.
examples.cn: 这款混合动力车两全其美，既环保又经济实惠。

examples.en: With this job, you get the best of both worlds: a good salary and flexible hours.
examples.cn: 有了这份工作，你可以两全其美：既有高薪水，又有灵活的工作时间。

origin.cn: 这个短语的意思是，从两种不同的情况或选择中获得最大的好处而没有任何负面影响。它最早可以追溯到19世纪，强调一种理想的、完美的状态，其中两种相对的事物能够和谐共存。

title: The best thing since sliced bread

definition.cn: 自切片面包以来最好的发明，用来形容某物非常棒或极其优秀。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the early 20th century when American inventor Otto Rohwedder invented the bread-slicing machine in 1928, making bread more popular and convenient. Since then, "sliced bread" has been seen as a major improvement, and the phrase has become a way to praise something as an outstanding new idea or invention.

examples.en: The new smartphone is considered the best thing since sliced bread.
examples.cn: 新的智能手机被认为是自切片面包以来最好的发明。

examples.en: He thinks his new software is the best thing since sliced bread.
examples.cn: 他认为他的新软件是自切片面包以来最好的东西。

examples.en: Everyone at the office says that new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.
examples.cn: 办公室的每个人都说那台新的咖啡机是自切片面包以来最好的东西。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪初，美国发明家奥托·罗维德于1928年发明了切片面包机，这使得面包在市场上更受欢迎和便利。从此，“切片面包” 被视为极大的改进，因此这个短语成了赞美某物非常出色的新创意或新发明的表达方式。

definition.cn: “纽约市”。
definition.en: This phrase can trace its origins back to the 1920s, when John J. Fitz Gerald, a sports writer for the New York Morning Telegraph, first used it in his horse-racing column to describe New York City as the ultimate goal and glory for horse races. Since the 1970s, the term has become even more popular due to the promotional efforts by the New York City tourism board.

examples.en: I've always dreamed of living in The Big Apple.
examples.cn: 我一直梦想着住在纽约市。

examples.en: They took a trip to The Big Apple to see a Broadway show.
examples.cn: 他们去了纽约市观看百老汇的演出。

examples.en: The Big Apple is known for its vibrant culture and diversity.
examples.cn: 纽约市以其充满活力的文化和多样性而闻名。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到1920年代，当时《纽约晨报》的体育记者John J. Fitz Gerald在他的赛马专栏中第一次使用了这个词语，来形容纽约市为赛马的终极目标和荣耀。从1970年代起，这一短语在纽约市旅游局的推广下变得更加广为人知。

definition.cn: “新奥尔良” 的昵称。这个短语用来描述美国路易斯安那州的新奥尔良市，因为该城市的生活节奏轻松悠闲，相比其他大城市，这里的压力较小。

examples.en: We decided to take a vacation in The Big Easy to enjoy some jazz music.
examples.cn: 我们决定去新奥尔良度假，享受一些爵士乐。

examples.en: Living in The Big Easy means you can always find great food and music.
examples.cn: 住在新奥尔良意味着你总能找到美食和音乐。

examples.en: He moved to The Big Easy for its vibrant cultural scene.
examples.cn: 他搬到新奥尔良是因为这里充满活力的文化氛围。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源尚不完全确定，但普遍认为是在1970年代，由记者们在描述新奥尔良的轻松氛围与文化时所使用的。新奥尔良以其独特的音乐、文化、食物和狂欢节（Mardi Gras）著称，所以 “*The Big Easy*” 形象地表达了这座城市的魅力。

definition.cn: “底线” 或 “最终结果”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from accounting, where it is used to refer to the final figure or net income, which appears on the last line of a profit-and-loss statement. In a broader sense, “the bottom line” is used to signify the core conclusion or most important fact of a matter or discussion.

examples.en: The bottom line is that we need to increase our sales to stay profitable.
examples.cn: 底线是我们需要增加销售才能保持盈利。

examples.en: The bottom line of the report is that our team performed well.
examples.cn: 报告的结论是我们的团队表现良好。

examples.en: You can offer all the excuses you want, but the bottom line is that the project is late.
examples.cn: 你可以找所有借口，但底线是项目已经拖延了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于会计学中，用于表示最终计算出的结论或净收益，即利润表中的最后一行。而在更广泛的使用中，“the bottom line” 被用来指代一个问题或讨论的核心结论或最重要的事实。

definition.cn: “男孩穿着蓝色制服”，意为 “警察”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the traditional blue uniforms worn by police officers in the United States and the United Kingdom. In modern contexts, "the boys in blue" is often used informally to refer to police officers, especially when talking about them while on duty.

examples.en: The neighborhood is safe thanks to the boys in blue patrolling every night.
examples.cn: 由于警察每晚巡逻，社区变得很安全。

examples.en: When trouble started, we called the boys in blue immediately.
examples.cn: 一有麻烦发生，我们立刻叫了警察来。

examples.en: He wanted to join the boys in blue and serve his community.
examples.cn: 他想加入警察队伍，为社区服务。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国和英国警察的传统制服，通常是蓝色的。在现代语境中，“the boys in blue” 常常用来非正式地指代警察，尤其是在谈论他们执行任务时。

definition.cn: “被冷落” 或 “被敷衍”。

examples.en: She gave him the brush-off when he asked her out.
examples.cn: 当他邀请她出去时，她冷淡地拒绝了他。

examples.en: I tried to help, but he just brushed me off.
examples.cn: 我试图帮忙，但他只是敷衍了事。

examples.en: Don't let her brush you off; make sure she listens to you.
examples.cn: 不要让她敷衍你；要确保她听你说。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于简单的身体动作，类似于用刷子把灰尘或杂质刷掉。当一个人被 “brush off” 时，就如同你把身上的灰尘轻轻刷掉一样，象征着对这人的轻视或不重视。因此，这个短语通常用来指被人冷落或敷衍了事，无论是口头上还是行为上的。

definition.cn: “迫切的问题” 或 “备受关注的问题”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the late 19th century, when "burning" was used to describe something particularly important or urgent. This vivid expression suggests that the issue is as pressing as a flame and needs immediate attention.

examples.en: The burning question is how we can solve the climate crisis.
examples.cn: 迫切的问题是我们如何解决气候危机。

examples.en: Let's address the burning question before moving on to the next topic.
examples.cn: 在进入下一个话题之前，我们先解决迫切的问题。

examples.en: Everyone in the meeting had the same burning question: when will the new project start?
examples.cn: 在会议上，所有人都有同样的迫切问题：新项目什么时候开始？

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到19世纪后期，当时人们用 “burning”（燃烧的）来形容特别重要或紧急的事情。这个形象的表达意味着这个问题如同火焰般迫切，需要立刻得到解决。

definition.cn: “最好的” 或者 “非常棒的”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 1920s USA, as one of the popular slang terms of the time. It was created by American journalist Tad Dorgan and became very popular for describing something or someone as the best or extremely good. Just as people find cats rare and intriguing, this idiom is used to describe something or someone as top-notch and exceptional.

examples.en: Her new dress is really the cat's meow; everyone loves it.
examples.cn: 她的新裙子真的非常棒；每个人都喜欢。

examples.en: The new restaurant in town is the cat's meow. The food is amazing!
examples.cn: 镇上的新餐厅真是顶尖的。食物太好吃了！

examples.en: If you think your new gadget is the cat's meow, I can't wait to see it!
examples.cn: 如果你认为你的新小玩意儿是最棒的，那我迫不及待想看到它！

origin.cn: “The cat's meow” 这个短语起源于20世纪20年代的美国，作为当时流行的俚语之一。这句话是由美国新闻人Tad Dorgan创建的，非常热门，用来形容某物或某人的绝佳之处。就像我们对猫咪感到稀有和惊奇一样，这个 idiom 用来形容某物或某人是顶尖的、出类拔萃的。

title: The devil is in the details

definition.cn: “细节决定成败” 或 “问题出在细节上”。
definition.en: This expression originates from the German phrase "Der Teufel steckt im Detail," which has been adopted into English. It emphasizes that even seemingly simple tasks can go wrong or fail if one does not pay attention to the details.

examples.en: We thought we had the project completed, but the devil is in the details.
examples.cn: 我们以为项目已经完成了，但问题出在细节上。

examples.en: The devil is in the details, so we need to review every part of the contract carefully.
examples.cn: 问题出在细节上，所以我们需要仔细审查合同的每一部分。

examples.en: When planning an event, remember that the devil is in the details.
examples.cn: 在策划活动时，记住细节决定成败。

origin.cn: 这个表达起源于德语的 “Der Teufel steckt im Detail” ，在英语中搬用了这种说法。它强调即使是看起来很简单的事情，如果不注意细节，也可能在细节上出问题或导致失败。

title: The early bird gets the worm

definition.cn: “早起的鸟儿有虫吃”。
definition.en: This proverb originates from the feeding habits of birds. Birds that wake up early are able to find food first. Therefore, this saying is used to imply that those who start early will have success or advantages, often used to encourage people to take action early and seize opportunities.

examples.en: She always arrives at the office before anyone else; the early bird gets the worm.
examples.cn: 她总是在其他人之前到达办公室，早起的鸟儿有虫吃。

examples.en: If you want the best deals, remember that the early bird gets the worm.
examples.cn: 如果你想要最好的交易，记得早起的鸟儿有虫吃。

examples.en: The early bird gets the worm, so I try to wake up at 5 AM every day.
examples.cn: 早起的鸟儿有虫吃，所以我每天都试图五点起床。

origin.cn: 这个谚语源自鸟类的早晨觅食习惯。早上早起的鸟儿会最先找到食物。因此，这句话用来比喻早早行动的人会获得成功或利益，常用来鼓励人们抓住机会，早些开始行动。

definition.cn: “显而易见却被人忽视的问题”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from an extreme situation where an elephant is in a room, but everyone pretends not to see it. It is mainly used to describe an obvious issue or fact that people choose to ignore because it is too awkward, sensitive, or complex. The use of this phrase reminds people that although big problems cannot be ignored, they are often cleverly avoided.

examples.en: We need to address the elephant in the room—why sales are declining.
examples.cn: 我们需要解决这个显而易见却被忽视的问题——为什么销售额在下降。

examples.en: Discussing layoffs is the elephant in the room that nobody wants to mention.
examples.cn: 谈论裁员是一个显而易见却被忽视的问题，没有人愿意提及。

examples.en: Financial troubles are the elephant in the room for many families.
examples.cn: 财务问题是许多家庭显而易见却被忽视的问题。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于一种极端的状况，即房间里有一只大象，但人们都假装看不见它。这主要用来形容一个显而易见的问题或事实，因为太过尴尬、敏感或复杂，人们选择避而不谈。该短语的使用提醒人们，虽然大的问题无法忽视，但却经常被巧妙地避开。

definition.cn: “在最后一刻” 或 “在最后关头”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Bible, specifically the book of Matthew, where a landowner hires workers at the eleventh hour. Hence, "the eleventh hour" evolved to describe a situation where something is done at the very last moment before a deadline or end.

examples.en: They presented their project at the eleventh hour.
examples.cn: 他们在最后一刻提交了他们的项目。

examples.en: I bought my plane ticket at the eleventh hour.
examples.cn: 我在最后关头买到了我的机票。

examples.en: The team managed to score a goal at the eleventh hour.
examples.cn: 球队在最后一刻设法进球了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自《圣经》中的《马太福音》章节，其中提到一个主人在第十一小时雇用了一些工人。由此产生了 “the eleventh hour” 这个短语，用以描述到一个事情即将截止或结束的最后时刻做某事的情景。

definition.cn: “伶牙俐齿” 或 “口才好”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Irish folklore, particularly the legend of the Blarney Stone. Supposedly, anyone who kisses the Blarney Stone is granted the gift of eloquence and persuasive ability. Hence, “the gift of the gab” is used to describe people who are articulate and persuasive speakers.

examples.en: John has the gift of the gab; he can persuade anyone to buy anything.
examples.cn: 约翰有伶牙俐齿的本领，他能说服任何人购买任何东西。

examples.en: She certainly possesses the gift of the gab, making her a great salesperson.
examples.cn: 她确实拥有伶牙俐齿的口才，使她成为一名出色的销售员。

examples.en: Not everyone has the gift of the gab, but it can be developed with practice.
examples.cn: 并不是每个人天生都有伶牙俐齿，但通过练习可以培养这种能力。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于爱尔兰神话，关于伯拉尼石（Blarney Stone）的传说。相传，亲吻伯拉尼石的人会获得某种特殊的能力，拥有出色的口才和说服力。因此，“the gift of the gab” 被用来形容那些善于表达、能言善辩的人。

definition.cn: “最后一刻” 或 “紧要关头”。
definition.en: This phrase metaphorically describes the scenario where time is almost running out, particularly when approaching a deadline or finishing a task. In modern English, "the last minute" is used to describe situations where something is completed or decided at the very last moment, often implying a sense of urgency or haste.

examples.en: He always does his homework at the last minute.
examples.cn: 他总是在最后一刻才做作业。

examples.en: The project was finished just in the last minute.
examples.cn: 这个项目是在最后一刻才完成的。

examples.en: She bought the tickets at the last minute.
examples.cn: 她在最后一刻才买了票。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于形象地描述时间快要用尽的情景，特别是即将到截止期限或完成某项任务的最后时刻。在现代英语中，“the last minute” 用来形容事情在最后关头才完成或者才决定的情况，常常包含紧张、仓促的含义。

definition.cn: “最大份额” 或 “最好的一部分”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a fable by the ancient Greek storyteller Aesop. In the fable, a lion, a fox, a wolf, and other animals hunt together, but the lion claims the best and largest portion of the prey for himself. This symbolizes that in power dynamics, the strongest often take the largest or best share.

examples.en: The manager took the lion's share of the credit for the project’s success.
examples.cn: 经理把项目成功的最大功劳占为己有。

examples.en: Despite the team's effort, the CEO received the lion's share of the profits.
examples.cn: 尽管团队付出了努力，CEO 却获得了最大的利润份额。

examples.en: He always insists on getting the lion's share of the inheritance.
examples.cn: 他总是坚持要得到遗产中最大的那一份。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于古希腊寓言作家伊索的故事。在这个寓言中，狮子、狐狸、狼和其他动物一起合作狩猎，但最终狮子声称自己应该得到最好的和最多的猎物。这也象征着在权力关系中，强者往往占据较大或最好的份额。

title: The long and short of it

definition.cn: “总之” 或 “长话短说”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from Shakespeare's play *The Merry Wives of Windsor*, where the original line is "this is the long and short of it", intending to cover both details and summary. Nowadays, this phrase is commonly used to sum up what has been said or to explain the main point of an event, serving as a succinct version of a longer explanation.

examples.en: The long and short of it is that we missed the deadline.
examples.cn: 总之，我们错过了截止日期。

examples.en: She gave a long explanation, but the long and short of it is that she can't come to the party.
examples.cn: 她做了很多解释，但总之她不能来参加聚会。

examples.en: The long and short of it is that we need more time to complete the project.
examples.cn: 长话短说，我们需要更多时间来完成这个项目。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于莎士比亚的戏剧《温莎的风流娘们》中，原文是 "this is the long and short of it"，意在将事情的详细和概要都涵盖进来。如今，这个短语主要用来总结之前所说的话或是解释事件的关键点，起到概括长篇叙述的作用。

definition.cn: “嘴馋” 或 “突然之间很想吃零食”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the depiction of a craving for food, especially referring to the sudden and intense desire to snack under certain conditions (such as the influence of specific drugs or emotional fluctuations). "Munchies" is a plural noun that emphasizes this impulse to eat snacks.

examples.en: After the party, everyone had the munchies and raided the fridge.
examples.cn: 聚会后，大家都突然嘴馋了，开始扫荡冰箱。

examples.en: He gets the munchies late at night and always eats a bowl of cereal.
examples.cn: 他晚上嘴馋，总是吃一碗麦片。

examples.en: I always carry some snacks in my bag in case I get the munchies.
examples.cn: 我总是在包里带些零食，以防止突然嘴馋。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于对食物渴望的形象化描述，尤其是指人在某些特定情况下（例如受到某些药物影响或情绪波动）突然产生的强烈进食欲望。“Munchies” 是一个复数形式的名词，强调了这种吃零食的冲动。

definition.cn: “前几天” 或 “不久前”。
definition.en: This idiom's exact origin is unclear, but it is widely used in spoken English to indicate that something happened fairly recently. It's a polite and commonly used phrase to talk about events in the recent past, which can refer to a few days ago, a week ago, or even slightly longer, depending on the context.

examples.en: I saw John at the grocery store the other day.
examples.cn: 前几天我在杂货店看到了约翰。

examples.en: The other day, I found an old photo album in the attic.
examples.cn: 前几天我在阁楼里找到了一本旧相册。

examples.en: We went out for dinner the other day and had a great time.
examples.cn: 前几天我们出去吃了晚饭，度过了一段美好时光。

origin.cn: 这个成语的确切来历已不可考，但它在口语中广泛使用，通常用来表示在不久前发生的事情。这是一个用来表述某件事在最近的过去发生的礼貌而常用的说法，可以指几天前、一周前甚至稍长一段时间前，具体取决于上下文。

definition.cn: “忍受极大的痛苦和麻烦的耐心”，或直译为 “约伯的耐心”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the story of Job in the Bible. Job was a devout believer who faced immense suffering and hardship but maintained his faith and patience without faltering. Therefore, "the patience of Job" is used to describe someone who can endure long-lasting difficulties without losing faith or complaining.

examples.en: He must have the patience of Job to deal with all those difficult clients.
examples.cn: 他一定有约伯的耐心，才能应付那些难缠的客户。

examples.en: Raising kids requires the patience of Job.
examples.cn: 养育孩子需要极大的耐心，简直需要约伯的耐心。

examples.en: You'd need the patience of Job to wait in this long queue.
examples.cn: 在这么长的队伍中等待，真的需要约伯的耐心。

origin.cn: 这个短语来自《圣经•约伯记》的故事。约伯是一个虔诚的信徒，他无论遇到多么巨大的痛苦和困境，仍然对上帝保持着坚定的信仰和极大的耐心。因此，“the patience of Job” 用来形容一个人能够忍受长期的困境，而不失去信心或抱怨。

definition.cn: “最糟糕的情况” 或 “绝望的境地”。
definition.en: This phrase comes from the literal meaning of "pits," which are dark, deep, and hard-to-escape places. This metaphorical usage signifies being in a very bad situation or experiencing something extremely unpleasant.

examples.en: That new restaurant is really the pits. The food was terrible.
examples.cn: 那家新餐馆真是糟糕透了。食物太差了。

examples.en: Missing the bus on a rainy day is just the pits.
examples.cn: 在雨天错过公共汽车真是糟糕透顶了。

examples.en: I got a flat tire on my way to an important meeting; it was the pits.
examples.cn: 在去参加重要会议的路上车胎爆了，真是太糟糕了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 “坑” 这个字面的意思，即一个黑暗、深而难以逃脱的地方。这个隐喻用法表示处于一个非常不好的情况或经历了非常不愉快的事情。

title: The pot calling the kettle black

definition.cn: “锅嫌壶黑” 或 “五十步笑百步”。
definition.en: This idiom dates back to the 17th century. Back then, people commonly used iron pots and kettles for cooking, which would turn black due to the soot from the fire. Thus, it is contradictory for a blackened pot to criticize a blackened kettle. This idiom is often used to describe someone accusing others of flaws or faults that they themselves possess.

examples.en: When John complained about Sarah being late, it was like the pot calling the kettle black - he's always late himself.
examples.cn: 当约翰抱怨萨拉迟到时，简直是锅嫌壶黑——他自己也总是迟到。

examples.en: Criticizing my spending habits is the pot calling the kettle black; you spend just as much as I do!
examples.cn: 批评我的消费习惯简直是五十步笑百步；你花的钱和我一样多！

examples.en: When she called him messy, it was the pot calling the kettle black. Her room is just as untidy.
examples.cn: 当她说他邋遢时，简直是锅嫌壶黑。她的房间也一样乱。

origin.cn: 这个成语的来源可以追溯到17世纪。当时，人们通常使用铁锅和铁壶作为炊具，它们在火上经过一段时间的使用后都会变黑。因此，当一只已经变黑的锅指责同样变黑的壶时，这种指责就是自相矛盾的。这一成语常用于形容某人指责别人的弱点或缺点，但自己也有同样的弱点或缺点。

definition.cn: “不寻常的选择” 或 “不同寻常的道路”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a poem by American poet Robert Frost titled "The Road Not Taken". In the poem, the poet chooses a less-traveled path, symbolizing his unusual and distinctive decisions in life. Nowadays, the phrase is used to describe choices or decisions that do not follow the conventional path, implying an adventurous, unique, or independent route.

examples.en: She took the road less travelled and started her own business instead of working for a big company.
examples.cn: 她选择了不寻常的道路，开始了自己的生意，而不是为大公司打工。

examples.en: Choosing the road less travelled often means facing more challenges, but can also lead to greater rewards.
examples.cn: 选择不寻常的道路往往意味着面临更多的挑战，但也可能带来更大的回报。

examples.en: He decided to take the road less travelled by moving to a small town and living off the grid.
examples.cn: 他决定选择不寻常的道路，搬到一个小镇并过上离网生活。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自美国诗人罗伯特 · 弗罗斯特（Robert Frost）的一首诗《未选择的路》（The Road Not Taken）。在这首诗中，诗人选择了一条较少人走的路，比喻他在生活中做出了不同寻常的决定。在现代使用中，这个短语用来描述那些不按照常规、不走寻常路的决定或选择，即选择冒险、独特或自己独创的路线。

definition.cn: “在同一频率上” 或 “有相同的想法或观点”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from radio communication technology, where two devices need to be on the same frequency to communicate with each other. In everyday usage, this phrase is metaphorically used to describe two or more people who are in agreement, share the same opinions or feelings, or understand each other very well.

examples.en: We always seem to be on the same wavelength during team projects.
examples.cn: 在团队项目中，我们似乎总是在同一个频率上。

examples.en: It's great to have a friend who is on the same wavelength as you.
examples.cn: 有一个和你在同一频率上的朋友真是太好了。

examples.en: The new manager and I are on the same wavelength about the project goals.
examples.cn: 新经理和我对项目目标意见一致。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于无线电通信技术，指两个设备在同一频率上才能相互通信。在日常用语中，这个短语用来比喻两个人或一群人之间达成一致，分享相同的观点或感觉，或彼此非常理解对方的意思。

definition.cn: “人生的挫折教育” 或 “社会大学”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the early 20th century and describes gaining life experience and wisdom through the hardships and challenges of real life, especially through failures and mistakes, rather than through formal schooling. It emphasizes the learning that comes from direct personal experience.

examples.en: He's a successful businessman who graduated from the school of hard knocks.
examples.cn: 他是一位在社会大学中历练成才的成功商人。

examples.en: She never went to college but learned everything she knows from the school of hard knocks.
examples.cn: 她从没上过大学，但所有的知识都是从人生挫折中学到的。

examples.en: Sometimes, the best education comes from the school of hard knocks.
examples.cn: 有时候，最好的教育来自于人生的挫折和教训。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪初，用以形容通过实际生活中的艰难和困苦，特别是失败和错误，而不是通过正规的学校教育来获取人生经验和智慧。它强调的是通过亲身经历而学到的人生教训。

title: The shoe is on the other foot

definition.cn: “换位思考” 或 “角色互换”。
definition.en: This idiom originated in the late 19th century and describes a situation where roles or positions are reversed. The original context referred to the discomfort or different experience when a shoe is on the other foot, since shoes were distinctly designed for the left and right foot. This expression has evolved to mean the reversal of roles or situations, often to emphasize understanding from another's perspective.

examples.en: Now that the shoe is on the other foot, he realizes how difficult her job was.
examples.cn: 现在角色互换了，他才意识到她的工作有多么困难。

examples.en: It feels weird when the shoe is on the other foot and you have to ask for help.
examples.cn: 当你需要请求帮助时，换位思考的感觉很奇怪。

examples.en: With the shoe on the other foot, she quickly changed her opinion about the policy.
examples.cn: 角色互换后，她很快对这个政策改变了看法。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早在19世纪后期出现，用来形容角色或立场的互换。最初的背景是指鞋子在另一只脚上，由于左右脚鞋子的形状不同，这种换位会引发不同的感受。不仅仅是角色的物理交换，这个表达还延伸出对立场和情景的反转，以便更好地理解对方的处境。

title: The short end of the stick

definition.cn: “吃亏” 或 “受到不平等对待”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from olden days when sticks were used in fights or disputes to judge who should be punished or blamed. Sometimes, a very short stick would be given to one side to symbolize that they were at a disadvantage or being treated unfairly. Over time, this idiom has come to be widely used to describe people being in a situation where they are at a disadvantage or unfairly treated.

examples.en: I really got the short end of the stick in that deal.
examples.cn: 在那笔交易中，我确实是吃亏了。

examples.en: She always seems to get the short end of the stick at work.
examples.cn: 她在工作中似乎总是受不平等对待。

examples.en: If you don't ask for what you deserve, you'll end up with the short end of the stick.
examples.cn: 如果你不争取应得的东西，你最终会吃亏的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古时候的斗殴或争端，人们常用棍子来评判谁该受到责罚或怪罪。有时候，有人会故意给一方一根很短的棍子，以表示他在争执中不占优势或者受到了不公平对待。渐渐地，这一短语就被广泛用于形容人们在某件事情中吃亏或受到不平等待遇。

title: The squeaky wheel gets the grease

definition.cn: “叫得响的轮子获得润滑” 或者 “会哭的孩子有奶吃”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the mechanical field, where a wheel that made a squeaky noise indicated it needed lubrication. Gradually, this phrase was borrowed to describe people who complain often or loudly tend to receive more attention and privileges. In modern society, it signifies that those who raise issues or complaints are more likely to have their problems addressed and receive help.

examples.en: If you want your request to be prioritized, remember: The squeaky wheel gets the grease.
examples.cn: 如果你想你的请求被优先处理，记住：会哭的孩子有奶吃。

examples.en: She always gets what she wants because she knows the squeaky wheel gets the grease.
examples.cn: 她总是能得到她想要的，因为她知道叫得响的轮子获得润滑。

examples.en: You should speak up about the problem; the squeaky wheel gets the grease.
examples.cn: 你应该说出这个问题；会哭的孩子有奶吃。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于机械领域，在早期的机器中，如果一个轮子发出吱吱声，意味着它需要润滑油。逐渐，这个短语被借用来形容那些爱抱怨的人往往能够得到更多的关注和优待。在现代社会中，用这个短语来表示那些抱怨或提出问题的人更容易得到解决和帮助。

definition.cn: “正道” 或 “正轨”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Bible, specifically Matthew 7:14, which states "narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life, and there are few who find it." Consequently, "the straight and narrow" is used to metaphorically describe someone adhering to moral and legal standards, following the righteous path, and avoiding wrongdoing.

examples.en: He's been on the straight and narrow ever since he left college.
examples.cn: 自从大学毕业后，他一直走在正道上。

examples.en: She managed to stay on the straight and narrow despite the temptations.
examples.cn: 尽管有许多诱惑，她还是设法保持在正轨上。

examples.en: Parents hope their children will remain on the straight and narrow as they grow up.
examples.cn: 父母希望孩子在成长过程中能一直走正道。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自《圣经》的《马太福音》7:14，其中提到 “门是窄的，路是小的，找到的人也不多”。因此，“the straight and narrow” 用来比喻一个人遵守道德规范和法律，走正道，避免不良行为。

definition.cn: “形势已经逆转” 或 “局势发生了变化”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the phenomenon of tides in oceanography. When the tide goes out or comes in, it signifies a noticeable change. Figuratively, this phrase is used to describe a significant shift in circumstances, often implying a change from a worse situation to a better one, or vice versa.

examples.en: The tide has turned, and now they are winning the match.
examples.cn: 形势已经逆转，他们现在正在赢得比赛。

examples.en: After months of struggle, the tide has turned for their business.
examples.cn: 经过几个月的挣扎，他们的生意终于好转了。

examples.en: I felt hopeless at first, but now it seems the tide has turned in my favor.
examples.cn: 一开始我感到绝望，但现在似乎形势对我有利了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来自海洋学中的潮汐现象。当潮水退去或涌来时，它标志着一个明显的变化。在比喻意义上，这个短语被用来形容事物发生了显著的变化，通常是从不利转向有利的变化或者相反。

definition.cn: “冰山一角”。
definition.en: This phrase draws from the physical property of icebergs, where only a small portion is visible above water, while the majority is hidden below the surface. Therefore, "the tip of the iceberg" is often used to convey that what is visible or known is only a small part of a larger, more complex issue or situation.

examples.en: The recent scandal is just the tip of the iceberg; there's a lot more we don't know yet.
examples.cn: 最近的丑闻只是冰山一角，还有更多我们不知道的事情。

examples.en: The financial losses reported are only the tip of the iceberg.
examples.cn: 报告的财务损失只是冰山一角。

examples.en: Her symptoms seemed mild, but they were just the tip of the iceberg.
examples.cn: 她的症状看起来轻微，但那只是冰山一角。

origin.cn: 这个短语借用了冰山的物理特性：只有一小部分漂浮在水面上，而大部分则隐藏在水面以下。因此，"the tip of the iceberg" 常用来表示某个问题或情况中仅显露出来的小部分，而更大的部分还未被察觉或展示出来。

definition.cn: “全力以赴” 或 “全部的”。
definition.en: The origin of this idiom is not definitive, but it generally means giving everything you have or using all available resources. One popular explanation is that during World War II, the length of the ammunition belts for aircraft machine guns was nine yards, and when pilots used all their ammunition, they had given it everything they had.

examples.en: When preparing for the presentation, she went the whole nine yards to make sure everything was perfect.
examples.cn: 为了准备这次演讲，她全力以赴确保一切都完美无缺。

examples.en: They decorated the house with the whole nine yards for the party.
examples.cn: 为了这次聚会，他们把房子装饰得无所不包。

examples.en: Our team went the whole nine yards to win the championship this year.
examples.cn: 我们的团队今年竭尽全力去赢得了冠军。

origin.cn: 这个成语的起源虽没有统一说法，但它通常表示你在做某件事时投入所有的努力和资源。一种比较流行的解释是，“the whole nine yards” 是指在二战期间，飞机上的机枪子弹带长度为九码，当飞行员用尽所有子弹时，就说明他们已经竭尽全力。

title: There are clouds on the horizon

definition.cn: “乌云压境” 或 “前景不妙”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the image of clouds appearing on the horizon, signifying an impending storm. Within this context, the phrase is used to describe signs of potential problems or difficulties in the future. It is often employed to convey concerns or foresight about potential issues or crises in the near future.

examples.en: With the economy slowing down, there are clouds on the horizon for many businesses.
examples.cn: 经济放缓意味着许多企业的前景不妙。

examples.en: The doctor's serious tone made it clear that there are clouds on the horizon regarding his health.
examples.cn: 医生严肃的语气显然预示着他的健康状况前景堪忧。

examples.en: Despite the current success, there are clouds on the horizon about the company's future.
examples.cn: 尽管目前很成功，但公司的未来前景不妙。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于乌云在地平线上出现的景象，意味着风暴即将来临。在此背景下，该短语被用来形容未来可能会出现问题或困难的迹象。它通常用于表达对未来某段时间内可能发生问题或危机的担忧或预感。

title: There are other fish in the sea

definition.cn: “天涯何处无芳草” 或 “海里还有别的鱼”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a fishing analogy, suggesting that in relationships or opportunities, even if one specific person or chance is lost, there are plenty of other options available. It is commonly used to comfort those who are heartbroken or have faced a setback in a significant relationship.

examples.en: Don't be so upset over a breakup; there are other fish in the sea.
examples.cn: 不要为分手太难过，天涯何处无芳草。

examples.en: He wasn't right for you anyway. Trust me, there are other fish in the sea.
examples.cn: 反正他不适合你。相信我，海里还有别的鱼。

examples.en: After losing that job opportunity, remember that there are other fish in the sea.
examples.cn: 在失去那个工作机会后，记得海里还有别的鱼。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于捕鱼的类比，表示在关系或机会中，即使失去了一个特定的人或机会，仍然有很多其他的选择。通常用于安慰那些在感情或其他重要关系中的失意者。

title: There's a method to his madness

definition.cn: “他看似疯狂，实际上有其道理” 或 “外表疯狂，实则有理”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from William Shakespeare's play "Hamlet." In the play, Polonius observes some of Hamlet's actions and comments with this phrase, suggesting that despite appearing mad, Hamlet's actions are purposeful and logical. In modern usage, the idiom generally refers to someone whose actions seem chaotic or absurd but actually have a well-thought-out rationale behind them.

examples.en: Don't worry about his strange work habits; there's a method to his madness.
examples.cn: 不用担心他奇怪的工作习惯；他看似疯狂，实际上有其道理。

examples.en: At first, her strategy seemed random, but soon I realized there was a method to her madness.
examples.cn: 起初，她的策略似乎很随意，但很快我就意识到她的外表疯狂，实则有理。

examples.en: Though his approach appeared chaotic, his results proved there's a method to his madness.
examples.cn: 尽管他的方法看起来很混乱，但结果证明他确实有其道理。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自威廉·莎士比亚的戏剧 《哈姆雷特》（Hamlet）。在剧中，波洛涅斯（Polonius）观察哈姆雷特（Hamlet）的一些行为后说出这句台词，暗示尽管哈姆雷特表现得疯狂，但他所为实际上有其目的和逻辑。在现代用法中，这个短语通常用来指某人看似无序或荒谬的行为，但实际上背后有着精心安排或合理的理由。

title: There's no such thing as a free lunch

definition.cn: “天下没有免费的午餐” 。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the early 20th century when some bars would offer a "free lunch" to attract patrons, but only if they bought drinks. In reality, the cost of the lunch was covered by the inflated price of the drinks. Hence, the expression conveys that nothing comes for free, and that seemingly free items often have hidden costs or conditions.

examples.en: Remember, there's no such thing as a free lunch; everything has a cost.
examples.cn: 记住，天下没有免费的午餐；一切皆有代价。

examples.en: The promotional offer looks good, but there's no such thing as a free lunch.
examples.cn: 这个促销看起来挺棒，但天下没有免费的午餐。

examples.en: When investing, always be cautious because there's no such thing as a free lunch.
examples.cn: 投资时一定要谨慎，因为天下没有免费的午餐。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪初，当时一些酒吧会提供免费的午餐以吸引顾客，但条件是他们必须买饮料。实际上，这些饮料的价格已经涵盖了午餐的成本。因此，这个表达告诉我们，世上没有真正的免费，即使看似免费的东西，往往隐藏着某种代价或附带条件。

definition.cn: “他们被匆忙地凑到一起” 或 “他们被仓促地安排在一起”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from situations where, due to sudden events or emergencies, people are rapidly assembled into a team or placed together. In these scenarios, individuals usually do not know each other well, and might come from different backgrounds or possess different skills, but they must collaborate because of a specific task or environment.

examples.en: During the emergency, they were thrown together to handle the crisis.
examples.cn: 在紧急情况下，他们被匆忙地凑到一起处理危机。

examples.en: The new project required people from different departments, so they were thrown together.
examples.cn: 新项目需要来自不同部门的人，因此他们被仓促地安排在一起。

examples.en: They were thrown together on the group project but ended up becoming good friends.
examples.cn: 他们被匆忙地凑到一起做小组项目，但最终成了好朋友。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于突发事件或紧急情况，需要快速组成一个团队或将一群人安排在一起。通常，这种情况下的人们并不熟悉对方，可能来自不同的背景或有不同的技能，但因为特定的任务或环境，他们不得不一起合作。

definition.cn: 跳出框框思考；打破常规思考。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 1970s to encourage people to avoid conventional thinking and approach problems in novel and creative ways. Later, it became widely used in business and innovation circles as a slogan to promote innovation and creative thinking.

examples.en: To solve this problem, you'll need to think outside the box.
examples.cn: 要解决这个问题，你需要跳出框框思考。

examples.en: Our company values employees who can think outside the box.
examples.cn: 我们公司重视那些能够打破常规思考的员工。

examples.en: Sometimes, the best solutions come from thinking outside the box.
examples.cn: 有时候，最好的解决方案来自打破常规的思考。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪70年代，用于鼓励人们在遇到问题时避免固有的思维模式，而是用新颖、创造性的方式去解决问题。后来，这句话被广泛应用于商业和创新领域，成为鼓励创新和创造性思维的口号。

definition.cn: “三次定律” 或 “第三次会有好运”。
definition.en: This phrase traces its origins back to ancient British culture, expressing the notion that success usually comes on the third try. This idea suggests that while the first two attempts might fail due to various reasons, the third attempt is often accompanied by good luck, leading to success. Hence, it is commonly used in contexts where persistence and continued effort after failure are encouraged.

examples.en: Don't worry if you didn't pass the exam this time. Remember, third time's a charm.
examples.cn: 不要担心这次没通过考试。记住，第三次会有好运的。

examples.en: He failed to climb the mountain twice, but third time's a charm he finally made it.
examples.cn: 他前两次爬山都失败了，但第三次他终于成功了。

examples.en: They lost their first two games, but they believe third time's a charm for their next match.
examples.cn: 他们前两场比赛输了，但他们相信下一场比赛会有好运的。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古老的英国，表达的是在第三次尝试通常会获得成功的观念。这种观念认为前两次尝试可能会因为各种原因失败，但第三次通常会有好运相伴，进而成功。因此，在遇到困难或失败后，鼓励继续尝试的语境中常会使用这个短语。

definition.cn: “这才是生活” 或 “这就是享受人生”。
definition.en: This phrase expresses a sense of contentment with the current moment, often said when enjoying good times or leisure activities. It conveys a sense feel relaxed, enjoyment, and happiness. This idiom can be traced back to early 20th century America, often used to describe an ideal or satisfying state of living.

examples.en: Sipping a cocktail by the beach, he sighed, "This is the life."
examples.cn: 在海滩边啜饮鸡尾酒，他叹道：“这才是生活。”

examples.en: After a long week, finally having a day off feels like, "This is the life."
examples.cn: 忙碌了一周后，终于迎来了休息日，感觉这才是生活。

examples.en: With a warm cup of coffee and a good book, she thought, "This is the life."
examples.cn: 捧着一杯热咖啡和一本好书，她心想：“这才是生活。”

origin.cn: 这个短语表达的是一种对当前时刻的满足感，通常是在享受美好时光或者休闲活动时所说的。它传递了一种放松、享受和幸福的情绪。这个成语最早可以追溯到20世纪初的美国，常常用来描述一种理想的或令人满意的生活状态。

title: Those who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones

definition.cn: “住在玻璃房子里的人不应该扔石头”，意思是人不要对别人进行批评，特别是当自己也有类似缺点或问题时。
definition.en: The phrase originates from an old proverb that serves to remind people to be cautious in criticizing or judging others, especially when they themselves may have similar flaws or vulnerabilities. It is often used to remind people to look at their own shortcomings before criticizing others.

examples.en: You shouldn't insult others about their behavior; those who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
examples.cn: 你不应该因为别人的行为而侮辱他们；住在玻璃房子里的人不应该扔石头。

examples.en: He always criticizes his colleagues, but those who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
examples.cn: 他总是批评他的同事，但住在玻璃房子里的人不应该扔石头。

examples.en: Before you judge me, remember that those who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
examples.cn: 在评判我之前，记住住在玻璃房子里的人不应该扔石头。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自古老的谚语，旨在提醒人们要谨慎对待对他人的批评和指责，因为自身可能也存在类似的缺点或易受攻击之处。这种表达常用于提醒人们在批评他人之前要先检讨自己。

definition.cn: “喝得酩酊大醉” 或 “烂醉如泥”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from 18th-century British nautical terminology. In sailing, a "sheet" does not refer to a bedsheet but to a rope that controls the sail. When three sheets are loose, the ship is hard to control and sways back and forth, much like a person who is heavily intoxicated and unsteady.

examples.en: He came home three sheets to the wind after the party.
examples.cn: 他在聚会后喝得烂醉如泥回了家。

examples.en: By midnight, most of the guests were three sheets to the wind.
examples.cn: 到午夜时，绝大部分客人都喝得酩酊大醉。

examples.en: You could tell he was three sheets to the wind just by looking at his stagger.
examples.cn: 只要看他摇摇晃晃的样子，你就知道他喝得烂醉如泥。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于18世纪英国航海术语。在航海中，“sheet” 并不是指床单，而是操控帆的绳索。当三条绳索都松开时，船容易失控，摇摆不定，通俗来说就是东倒西歪。因此，形容一个人醉酒得控制不住自己，就像失控的船一样。

definition.cn: “让我大吃一惊” 或 “让我措手不及”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from boxing and Western colloquial expressions, where "loop" refers to a circling or spinning motion. When someone's expectations are drastically overturned or something surprising happens, they feel like they've been "spun" or "looped". Therefore, "threw me for a loop" signifies a situation where someone is greatly surprised or caught off guard.

examples.en: The sudden resignation of our manager threw me for a loop.
examples.cn: 我们经理的突然辞职让我大吃一惊。

examples.en: His unexpected confession really threw me for a loop.
examples.cn: 他意外的告白让我措手不及。

examples.en: I was thrown for a loop when they announced the merger.
examples.cn: 当他们宣布合并时，我感到非常意外。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自拳击和西方口语中，"loop"指的是一个环绕或旋转的动作。当某人的预期被剧烈地颠覆，或者发生了令人惊讶的事情，他们就有了被 “环绕” 或 “旋转” 的感觉。因此，“threw me for a loop” 表示让一个人感到非常意外和措手不及的情况。

definition.cn: “同甘共苦” 或 “风雨无阻”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from medieval England, where it referred to the dense (thick) and sparse (thin) parts of a forest, signifying that one will go through any difficulties or favorable circumstances together. In modern English, "through thick and thin" is used to denote steadfast support and loyalty through any hardship or challenge, particularly in interpersonal relationships.

examples.en: They have been friends through thick and thin for over twenty years.
examples.cn: 他们已经同甘共苦了二十多年。

examples.en: A true partner will stand by you through thick and thin.
examples.cn: 一个真正的伴侣会在风雨无阻地支持你。

examples.en: Despite all the challenges, he remained loyal through thick and thin.
examples.cn: 尽管面临各种挑战，他始终如一地忠诚。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自中世纪的英国，最早指的是森林中的浓密（thick）和稀疏（thin）部分，表示无论穿过怎样的困难或顺境，人们都会一起走过去。在现代英文中，“through thick and thin” 用来表示无论面临多大的困难或挑战，都会坚持到底，尤指人际关系中的相互支持和忠诚。

definition.cn: “出其不意” 或 “制造意外”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from baseball, where a curveball has an unpredictable trajectory that can catch the batter off guard. In everyday life, "throw a curveball" describes a situation where someone presents an unexpected problem or surprise that disrupts plans or catches others unprepared.

examples.en: The boss threw a curveball by changing the project deadline at the last minute.
examples.cn: 老板在最后一刻突然改变项目截止日期，让人措手不及。

examples.en: Just when we thought the meeting was over, he threw a curveball with a new proposal.
examples.cn: 就在我们以为会议结束时，他突然提出了一项新提议，让人措手不及。

examples.en: Life can throw you a curveball, so it's always good to have a backup plan.
examples.cn: 生活中总会有意外，因此最好准备一个备用计划。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自棒球运动中的曲线球（curveball），这种球的轨迹难以预测，会让击球手措手不及。在日常生活中，“throw a curveball” 用来形容某人给别人出难题或制造意外的状况，使人措手不及或打乱计划。

title: Throw a monkey wrench into the works

definition.cn: “搅局” 或 “破坏计划”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a real tool in American industrial history, the "monkey wrench." If the tool was thrown into a working machine, it would cause the machine to stop or be damaged. Consequently, this phrase metaphorically evolved to describe any action that disrupts or sabotages plans or ongoing processes, whether intentionally or accidentally.

examples.en: His sudden resignation really threw a monkey wrench into the works of our project.
examples.cn: 他的突然辞职真是我么项目里的大搅局。

examples.en: The bad weather threw a monkey wrench into the works of our outdoor event schedules.
examples.cn: 恶劣天气破坏了我们户外活动的安排。

examples.en: Technical issues threw a monkey wrench into the works of the live broadcast.
examples.cn: 技术问题让直播出了乱子。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国工业历史中的一个真实工具，即 “猴子扳手（monkey wrench）”。如果把这个工具扔进运转的机器里，势必会导致机器停工或损坏。因此，这个表达逐渐演变为比喻任何故意或无意中破坏已经计划好或正在进行的事情的行为。

definition.cn: “不顾后果” 或 “抛开谨慎”。
definition.en: This phrase first appeared in the 19th century, indicating a person is ready to abandon caution and take some risks or bold actions. Literally, it means "throwing caution to the wind," letting the wind blow it away, thus completely ignoring the consequences and choosing to act in a bold or unconventional manner.

examples.en: Sometimes you just have to throw caution to the wind and try something new.
examples.cn: 有时候你必须不顾后果，尝试一些新的东西。

examples.en: They decided to throw caution to the wind and invest all their savings in the new venture.
examples.cn: 他们决定抛开谨慎，将所有积蓄投资在这个新项目上。

examples.en: Let’s throw caution to the wind and go on a spontaneous road trip this weekend.
examples.cn: 让我们不顾后果，这个周末去一次即兴公路旅行吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早出现在19世纪，表明一个人放弃小心谨慎，准备冒一定的风险或采取大胆的行动。字面意思是将 ‘谨慎’ 丢向风中，让风把它吹走，即完全不顾及后果，转而采取大胆的或非传统的方式行事。

definition.cn: “被抛给狼群” 或 “被推入险境”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from ancient tales or stories where a person thrown to the wolves is placed in extreme danger or abandoned in a hostile and harsh environment, forced to face all challenges and threats alone. In modern English, the idiom is used to describe someone who is put in a very difficult situation without support.

examples.en: After only a week of training, he was thrown to the wolves and had to handle the project alone.
examples.cn: 仅仅培训了一周，他就被推入险境，必须独自处理这个项目。

examples.en: New employees often feel like they’ve been thrown to the wolves without proper guidance.
examples.cn: 新员工常常觉得自己在没有得到适当指导的情况下被推入险境。

examples.en: She felt like she was thrown to the wolves when she had to present in front of the entire board.
examples.cn: 她感到被推入险境，因为她必须在整个董事会面前做展示。

origin.cn: 这个成语源于古老的传说或故事，当一个人处于极端危险的境地或被抛弃在敌对和恶劣的环境中时，就像被抛给狼群一样，被迫独自应对所有挑战和威胁。在现代英语中，这个成语用来形容某人被置于极端困难和无需帮助的状况下。

definition.cn: “非常高兴” 或 “乐得合不拢嘴”。
definition.en: This idiom doesn't have a precise origin but can be traced back to the early 20th century. Etymologists suggest that the expression comes from the idea that when people are very happy or delighted, their faces might develop a pinkish blush, hence "tickled pink." It is used to describe an extreme state of happiness or delight.

examples.en: She was tickled pink when she found out she had won the contest.
examples.cn: 她得知自己赢得比赛时，开心得不得了。

examples.en: I'm tickled pink to see you here tonight!
examples.cn: 今晚见到你，我高兴极了！

examples.en: They were tickled pink with their new puppy.
examples.cn: 他们对新小狗高兴得合不拢嘴。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来历并无确切的出处，但可以追溯到20世纪早期。词源学家推测该表达法源于当人们非常开心或受宠若惊时，脸上会泛起一种红晕，这种颜色与粉色相似，因此得名 “tickled pink”。这个表达法常用于描述极其愉快、非常开心的情感状态。

definition.cn: “勒紧裤腰带” 或 “紧缩生活”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from periods of economic hardship when people had to cut down on food to save money, leading them to tighten their belts as they lost weight. In modern society, "tighten your belt" or "belt-tightening" has become a common expression to describe a frugal lifestyle adopted to cope with financial difficulties.

examples.en: In tough times, everyone has to tighten their belts a little.
examples.cn: 在艰难时期，每个人都必须稍微勒紧裤腰带。

examples.en: The company is going through a slow season, so there will be some belt-tightening measures.
examples.cn: 公司正在经历一个淡季，所以会有一些紧缩措施。

examples.en: After losing his job, he had no choice but to tighten his belt until he found new work.
examples.cn: 失业后，他别无选择，只能勒紧裤腰带，直到找到新工作。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于经济困难时期，人们为了节省开支，需要减少饮食，进而需要勒紧腰带以适应体型的缩小。在现代社会，“tighten your belt” 或 “belt-tightening” 已经成为了描述一种为了应对经济困难而采取的节俭生活方式的常用表达。

definition.cn: “与风车作斗争” 或 “庸人自扰”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from Miguel de Cervantes' novel "Don Quixote." In the novel, Don Quixote mistakes windmills for giants and attacks them, resulting in a futile effort. The phrase is used to describe a situation where someone is attacking imaginary enemies or pursuing a vain and futile course of action, signifying a waste of energy on pointless endeavors.

examples.en: He's always tilting at windmills instead of solving real problems.
examples.cn: 他总是与风车作斗争，而不是解决真正的问题。

examples.en: Arguing with him about that old theory is just tilting at windmills.
examples.cn: 跟他争论那个陈旧的理论只是在庸人自扰。

examples.en: Stop tilting at windmills and focus on what's important.
examples.cn: 别再庸人自扰了，专注于重要的事情。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自米格尔·德·塞万提斯撰写的小说《堂吉诃德》。在小说中，堂吉诃德将风车误认为巨人，并向它们发起攻击，最终徒劳无功。这个短语用来形容那些攻击或对抗想象中的敌人或毫无意义的目标，通常表示一种浪费精力的愚蠢行为。

title: Time flies when you're having fun

definition.cn: “快乐时光总是过得特别快” 或 “快乐的时光总是稍纵即逝”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the feeling that time seems to pass quickly when people are engaged in enjoyable activities. Conversely, if people are involved in boring or unpleasant tasks, time appears to drag on. This saying is often used to describe the perception that time flies during enjoyable events.

examples.en: We were at the theme park all day, and it felt like minutes. Time flies when you're having fun.
examples.cn: 我们在游乐园玩了一整天，感觉就像几分钟一样。快乐时光总是过得特别快。

examples.en: Time flies when you're having fun; I can't believe the weekend is over already.
examples.cn: 快乐的时光总是稍纵即逝；我简直不敢相信周末已经结束了。

examples.en: She couldn't believe how quickly her vacation ended. Time flies when you're having fun.
examples.cn: 她不敢相信她的假期已经结束了。快乐时光总是过得特别快。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于一种感受，即当人们享受某个令人愉快的活动时，时间似乎会过得飞快。反之，如果人们从事无聊或不喜欢的事情，时间就会显得特别漫长。这句话通常用于描述在愉快的活动中感觉时间过得特别快的情景。

definition.cn: “时间就是金钱”。
definition.en: The phrase's origin can be traced back to the 18th century, introduced by American statesman and scientist Benjamin Franklin in his essay "Advice to a Young Tradesman". He emphasized the importance of time and its relation to wealth. Today, it is a common idiom used to advise people to value their time, avoid wasting it, to achieve success and wealth.

examples.en: In business, time is money, so we can't afford to waste any.
examples.cn: 在商业中，时间就是金钱，所以我们不能浪费任何时间。

examples.en: When you're billing clients by the hour, time is money.
examples.cn: 当你按小时收费时，时间就是金钱。

examples.en: Let's not delay the project any longer. Remember, time is money.
examples.cn: 我们不要再拖延项目了。记住，时间就是金钱。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来源可以追溯到18世纪，由美国的政治家、科学家本杰明·富兰克林（Benjamin Franklin）在他的文章《Advice to a Young Tradesman》 强调时间的重要性及其与财富的关系而提出。这个短语如今已成为一个常用成语，用来劝告人们要珍惜时间，避免浪费，以赢得成功和财富。

title: To be a chicken / to chicken out

definition.cn: “胆小鬼” 或 “临阵退缩”。
definition.en: The phrase "to be a chicken" means to describe someone as being very cowardly, often used to mock those who back down in the face of danger or difficulty. It originates from the behavior of chickens, which are easily frightened and tend to run away. "To chicken out" means to back out or give up at the last moment, specifically indicating someone who originally planned to do something but then decides not to because of fear or nervousness.

examples.en: Don't be a chicken—just try the rollercoaster!
examples.cn: 别当胆小鬼——试一试过山车吧！

examples.en: He wanted to ask her out, but he chickened out at the last moment.
examples.cn: 他本来想约她出去，但在最后一刻却临阵退缩了。

examples.en: I'm not going to chicken out now; I've come too far.
examples.cn: 我现在不会临阵退缩，我已经走了这么远了。

origin.cn: “to be a chicken” 的意思是形容某人很胆小，常用来讽刺那些在危险或困难面前退缩的人。这个说法源自鸡这种动物，它们通常容易受到惊吓而逃跑。而 “to chicken out” 的意思是指某人在关键时刻退缩或放弃，具体指那个人本来打算做某事但最后因为害怕或胆怯而放弃。

definition.cn: “极度激动” 或 “极度愤怒、悲伤”。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to Middle English, meaning a person is in an extreme state of emotion, making them feel like they are outside of themselves and unable to control their feelings. This state is similar to a mental separation, indicating that people are overwhelmed by emotions to the point of losing self-control.

examples.en: She was beside herself when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 当她听到这个消息时，她几乎无法自控。

examples.en: He was beside himself with rage after the argument.
examples.cn: 争论之后，他愤怒得几乎要失去理智。

examples.en: The mother was beside herself with worry when her child went missing.
examples.cn: 当孩子失踪时，母亲忧虑得几乎无法自持。

origin.cn: 这个表达的历史可以追溯到中古英语，意为一个人处于情绪的极端，使得他们感觉像是处于情绪之外，无法控制自己。这种状态类似于一种精神上的分离，表明人们被情感所淹没，以至于无法自我约束。

definition.cn: “吝啬” 或 “小气”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from a vivid metaphor of a tightly clenched fist, indicating a reluctance to spend money or an extremely frugal attitude. It is used in everyday life to describe people who are very careful with their money, often to the point of being miserly.

examples.en: He's so closefisted that he never tips the waiter.
examples.cn: 他非常小气，从来不给服务员小费。

examples.en: My closefisted neighbor never donates to charity.
examples.cn: 我那吝啬的邻居从不捐款给慈善机构。

examples.en: It’s difficult to be friends with someone so closefisted.
examples.cn: 和一个如此吝啬的人做朋友是很困难的。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于形象的比喻，即紧握拳头不肯放开，象征着不愿意花钱或很谨慎地控制自己的开支。在日常生活中，用来形容那些在金钱上非常节俭，甚至过于吝啬的人。

definition.cn: “很有钱” 或 “财大气粗”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a figurative description of wealth, implying that a person is carrying so much fortune that they are metaphorically "loaded" with it. Over time, this phrase has come to be used to describe individuals who are very wealthy.

examples.en: After selling his startup, he's completely loaded.
examples.cn: 卖掉他的初创公司后，他彻底变得很有钱了。

examples.en: Don’t worry about the cost; he's loaded.
examples.cn: 不用担心开销，他很有钱。

examples.en: They must be loaded if they can afford such a house.
examples.cn: 如果他们能买得起这样的房子，那他们一定很有钱。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于对财富的形象描述，意指一个人携带了大量的财富，重得如同 “装满” 了一样，因此是 “实至名归” 的富有。随着时间的推移，这个短语就被大家用来形容那些财力雄厚的人。

definition.en: This phrase means that someone or something is given a name derived from another person or thing. This idiom originates as a way to honor or memorialize a person or thing by naming something new after them.

examples.en: She was named after her grandmother.
examples.cn: 她以她祖母的名字命名。

examples.en: The new building was named after the founder of the company.
examples.cn: 新大楼是以公司创始人的名字命名的。

examples.en: He found out that he was named after a famous author.
examples.cn: 他发现自己是以一位著名作家的名字命名的。

origin.cn: 这个短语指的是某人或某物是以另一个人或事物的名字命名的。这个惯用语来源于一种尊敬或纪念某个人或事物的方式，以他们的名字来命名新的事物或人的过程。

title: To be out of the question

definition.cn: “不可能的” 或 “不在考虑范围之内”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the literal translation "to be away from the question," meaning that something is not even being considered as a possibility. It is used to describe situations or matters that are completely unachievable or out of the realm of possibility. It can be used in both formal and informal contexts.

examples.en: Buying a new car this year is out of the question; we just can't afford it.
examples.cn: 今年买新车是不可能的；我们实在负担不起。

examples.en: Skipping the final exam is simply out of the question if you want to pass the course.
examples.cn: 如果你想通过这门课程，缺席期末考试是不可能的事情。

examples.en: Asking for a significant raise during the budget cuts is out of the question.
examples.cn: 在削减预算期间要求大幅加薪是不在考虑范围之内的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于直译中的 “离开了问题”，指的是某件事情或状态根本不是问题的一部分，因而被排除在讨论或考虑之外。它用于描述那些完全无法实现或超出可能性的事情，在许多正式和非正式场合均可使用。

title: To be tied up with something or someone

definition.cn: “与某事或某人有紧密联系” 或 “忙于某事或某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the physical concept of being tied up, meaning being restrained by something or someone. In modern English, this phrase is widely used to indicate that someone is very busy or preoccupied with something or someone, to the point of being unable to focus on other matters.

examples.en: I'm tied up with work right now and can't meet for lunch.
examples.cn: 我现在被工作缠住了，无法去吃午饭。

examples.en: She’s tied up with her kids all day.
examples.cn: 她整天都在忙着照顾孩子。

examples.en: He's been tied up with a big project lately.
examples.cn: 他最近一直忙于一个大项目。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于物理上被捆绑的概念，表示被一件事情或一个人牵制住，无法脱身。在现代英语中，这个短语被广泛使用来表示一个人因某事或某人而非常忙碌或被占用了大部分时间。

definition.cn: “正在忙某事” 或 “在策划什么事情（通常指不太好的事情）”。
definition.en: This idiom is often used to describe someone who is engaged in some activity, especially when suspected of planning or doing something secretive or not entirely good. The exact origin of this phrase is unclear, but in everyday communication, it's commonly used to express suspicion or curiosity about someone's actions.

examples.en: I think the kids are up to something in the backyard.
examples.cn: 我觉得孩子们在后院忙着什么。

examples.en: He’s been acting strange lately; I wonder if he’s up to something.
examples.cn: 他最近行为古怪，我怀疑他在策划什么。

examples.en: Whenever John is quiet, you know he is up to something.
examples.cn: 每当约翰安静的时候，你就知道他在偷偷做什么事情。

origin.cn: 这个短语常常用来形容某人正在忙于某些事情，特别是当被认为可能在计划或进行一些秘密或不太好的行为时。这个短语的确切起源不明，但在日常交流中，它常用来表达对某人行为的怀疑或好奇。

definition.cn: “非常响亮” 或 “非常强调地”。
definition.en: The phrase originates from early American slang, meaning to do something very intensely, exceedingly, or exceptionally, almost to the extent of overshadowing a band's noise. It is most often used to describe very loud sounds, vigorous actions, or extremely intensive activities.

examples.en: The kids were shouting and laughing to beat the band.
examples.cn: 孩子们又叫又笑，非常响亮。

examples.en: He was running to beat the band, trying to catch the bus.
examples.cn: 他拼命地跑，试图赶上公交车。

examples.en: They celebrated to beat the band when their team won the championship.
examples.cn: 当他们的球队夺冠时，他们庆祝得非常热烈。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于早期的美国俚语，意思是做某事非常激烈、极端或出色，以至于几乎要盖过乐队的声音。这个短语最常用在描述声音、动作或活动非常激烈的场合。

definition.cn: “借他人的耳朵” 或 “向某人唠叨”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from English and describes someone talking persistently to another, often for a long period, usually to complain or vent. This behavior can often make the listener feel annoyed or helpless.

examples.en: He wouldn't stop bending my ear about the lousy service he received.
examples.cn: 他不停地向我唠叨他所遭遇的糟糕服务。

examples.en: Whenever she has a problem, she always bends my ear for hours.
examples.cn: 每当她有问题时，她总是向我唠叨好几个小时。

examples.en: I hate when people try to bend my ear about things I have no control over.
examples.cn: 我讨厌人们试图向我唠叨那些我无法控制的事情。

origin.cn: 这个成语起源于英语，描述某人不停地跟另一个人说话，尤其是延续很长时间，通常是为了抱怨或倾诉。这种行为可能让人感到烦扰或者无奈。

definition.cn: “失去知觉” 或 “临时断电”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from two main contexts: one is when a person temporarily loses consciousness or memory due to reasons like drunkenness, extreme fatigue, or medical issues; the other is when there is a blackout and the entire area becomes dark. In both scenarios, the emphasis is on sudden and temporary loss of awareness or visibility.

examples.en: He blacked out after drinking too much at the party.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上喝得太多而失去知觉。

examples.en: The street blacked out during the storm last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚的暴风雨使整条街断电变黑。

examples.en: She blacked out during her presentation due to stage fright.
examples.cn: 她因为怯场在做报告时失去了知觉。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于两个主要场景: 一是人因某些原因 （例如酗酒、极端疲劳或医疗问题） 短暂失去知觉或记忆；二是在停电的时候，整个区域变黑。无论是何种情况，都强调突然和暂时地失去知觉或视力。

definition.cn: “自吹自擂” 或 “自我吹嘘”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from medieval European military and noble culture, where horns were used to announce someone's arrival. In modern English, the idiom is used to describe someone who overly emphasizes their skills, achievements, or virtues, displaying a boastful attitude.

examples.en: You shouldn’t always blow your own horn; let others praise you.
examples.cn: 你不应该总是自吹自擂；让别人来夸赞你吧。

examples.en: He's constantly blowing his own horn about his sales record.
examples.cn: 他总是自吹自擂他的销售记录。

examples.en: The manager blew his own horn during the meeting, which annoyed everyone.
examples.cn: 经理在会议上自吹自擂，这让所有人都感到厌烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于欧洲中世纪的军队和贵族文化，当时用号角来宣布某人的到来。在现代英语中，这个成语用来指某人过度强调自己的能力、成就或优点，表现出一种自夸的态度。

definition.cn: “失败” 或 “惨遭失败”。该用语通常用于描述电影、戏剧、演出或其他类似项目在票房或评价上的失败。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the early 20th-century American theater scene. When a play or performance failed miserably, attracting few audiences and receiving poor reviews, it was described as a "bomb," akin to an unexpected explosion. "To bomb" evolved into a specialized term to indicate a complete failure, particularly widely used in the entertainment industry.

examples.en: The new movie bombed at the box office.
examples.cn: 这部新电影在票房上惨遭失败。

examples.en: His presentation bombed and no one was impressed.
examples.cn: 他的演讲彻底失败，没有人印象深刻。

examples.en: The band's latest album bombed despite the hype.
examples.cn: 尽管宣传很多，这支乐队的最新专辑却惨遭失败。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 20 世纪初期的美国剧院界。当一部戏剧或一场演出彻底失败，观众少而且评价极差时，就会被形容为 “炸弹”，好像突然爆炸一样。“To bomb” 进而演变成了表示某件事情或事件大获失败的专门表达，特别是在娱乐行业中广泛使用。

definition.cn: “使某人走投无路” 或 “困住某人”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the boxing world, where a strategy involves cornering the opponent to limit their movement. In everyday life, it's used to describe a situation where someone is left with no options or way out due to strategic actions or constraints.

examples.en: They tried to box him in during the meeting, forcing him to agree to their terms.
examples.cn: 他们在会议中试图困住他，迫使他同意他们的条件。

examples.en: She felt boxed in by the company's strict policies.
examples.cn: 她觉得被公司的严格政策所困住了。

examples.en: The lack of funding boxed us in and halted the project's progress.
examples.cn: 资金不足使我们走投无路，项目进展因此停滞。

origin.cn: 这个习语源自拳击运动中的 “围困” 策略，即把对手逼到角落，限制他们的行动自由。在现实生活中，该短语常用来形容通过策略或手段使某人没有其他选择或出路。

definition.cn: “烦扰某人” 或 “使某人心烦”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the slang word "bug," which literally means a small insect, but has been extended to mean persistent disturbance or annoyance. Figuratively, it is akin to being constantly bitten or bothered by bugs, leading to considerable annoyance. Therefore, "to bug someone" means to continuously disturb or bother someone in a way that makes them irritated.

examples.en: Can you stop asking me questions? You're starting to bug me.
examples.cn: 你能不能别再问我问题了？你开始让我烦了。

examples.en: Her habit of tapping the pen on the table really bugs me.
examples.cn: 她敲桌子的习惯真的让我很烦。

examples.en: It bugs me when people don't clean up after themselves.
examples.cn: 当人们不收拾自己的东西时，我很烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于俚语 “bug”，原意为小虫子，引申为不断干扰或烦扰的意思。形象地说，就像小虫子不断地叮咬，让人非常烦躁不安。因此，"to bug someone" 就是指不停地打扰某人或者做一些让对方感到厌烦的事情。

definition.cn: “插嘴” 或 “插手”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the term "butt," meaning to strike with the head or horns. "To butt in" is commonly used to describe someone who intrudes into a conversation or affair without being invited, often in an unwelcome manner. This expression has become particularly prevalent to describe interruptions or interference at inappropriate times or settings.

examples.en: Please don't butt in while we're talking.
examples.cn: 请不要在我们说话时插嘴。

examples.en: She tends to butt in on other people's business.
examples.cn: 她总是喜欢插手别人的事情。

examples.en: It's rude to butt in when someone else is speaking.
examples.cn: 在别人说话时插嘴是不礼貌的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 “butt”，意思是用头或角撞击。而 "to butt in" 通常用来描述某人不请自来地进入谈话或事务中，通常是不受到欢迎的情况。这个表达变得特别普遍，用来形容在不适当的时间或场合打断或干涉他人的行为。

definition.cn: “收工” 或 “今天到此为止”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from workers who would announce the end of their workday. In modern usage, it means someone is deciding to stop the current work or activity, usually after completing a task or reaching a milestone.

examples.en: After fixing the last bug, we decided to call it a day and go home.
examples.cn: 修复了最后一个漏洞之后，我们决定收工回家。

examples.en: It's getting late, let's call it a day and continue tomorrow.
examples.cn: 时间不早了，今天咱们就到此为止，明天再继续吧。

examples.en: We didn't finish the project, but we were tired and decided to call it a day.
examples.cn: 我们没有完成项目，但我们都很累了，所以决定今天就到此为止。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于劳动者在结束一天的劳动后宣布当天的工作结束。在现代英语中的用法，表示某人决定停止当前的工作或活动，不再继续，通常会在完成一个任务或达到阶段性目标后使用。

title: To call someone on the carpet

definition.cn: “训斥某人” 或 “责怪某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from early 19th-century Britain. At that time, "carpet" referred to the carpeted office of a high-ranking official. When an employee was called to the superior's carpeted office, it usually meant they were about to be reprimanded or punished. Thus, "to call someone on the carpet" means to be scolded by a superior or authority figure.

examples.en: The manager called him on the carpet for missing the deadline.
examples.cn: 经理因为他错过了最后期限而训斥了他。

examples.en: She was called on the carpet for her poor performance at work.
examples.cn: 由于工作表现差，她被责骂了一顿。

examples.en: After the error in the report, he knew he would be called on the carpet by his boss.
examples.cn: 报告中出现错误后，他知道他会被老板训斥。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早起源于19世纪初的英国。在那时，“carpet” 指的是高级官员办公室里的地毯。当员工被召唤到上司铺有地毯的办公室时，通常意味着他们将被训斥或惩罚。因此，“to call someone on the carpet” 意味着被上司或权威人士训斥。
